purpose: Select one economically interpretable Campaign029 mechanism without opening a Campaign029 minute partition, market benchmark value, candidate value, comparison value, daily price, or forward return.

selected_concept.economic_question: Does a stock's one-minute price-adjustment magnitude repeatedly rise and fall with the magnitude of same-minute market-wide shocks after removing the stock from the market benchmark?
selected_concept.economic_hypothesis: Lower synchronization with same-minute market shock magnitudes can represent less crowded liquidity demand and lower common-shock fragility. A directionally higher decoupling score may therefore be associated with better resilience from the next open through the third close.
selected_concept.fixed_temporal_question: Use the 119 adjacent close returns inside 09:31-11:30 and the 119 adjacent close returns inside 13:01-15:00. Match each stock return to the same fixed return position of its leave-one-out market mean. Exclude standalone 09:30, lunch, overnight, cross-day, cross-stock, lead-lag, and cross-half transitions.
known_design_risks: absolute versus squared returns, correlation versus regression, direction, exact-zero retention, peer threshold, and half-session boundary are researcher degrees of freedom unless frozen before values
the candidate may be statistically associated with signed market dependence or within-stock volatility-clustering factors even though it measures a different same-minute magnitude relation
low market-shock synchronization may mean resilience or simply weak information incorporation, so the higher-decoupling direction must be frozen before returns
using signed returns, market-return signs, leads or lags, subwindows, amount or volume weights, daily fields, terminal factor values, or cross-sectional return dispersion would change the mechanism

rejected_concepts.reason: This was explicitly rejected by Campaign028 scouting as too close to terminal return-sign-run and bar-direction-continuity families and is not reopened.

This is economically interesting but needs a newly materialized return-squared benchmark and a second heavy full-source pass. The same-minute market-shock magnitude question can be isolated with the already-frozen leave-one-out sum/count benchmark.
Signed same-minute correlation, residual drift, lead-lag asymmetry, and market-sign-conditioned dependence are already terminal historical families.
Campaign029 must be one new raw stock-plus-market statistic; combining, inverting after results, filtering, or rescuing terminal factors is prohibited.
